title: Meier et al. (2016): Short-answer practice
instructions: Answer in English with a concise concept or number. Theme percentages describe the articles in each perspective group, rather than the percentage of all individual patients, relatives, or professionals.

items.question: Which two databases were searched for this review?
items.explanation: The search extended from database inception through November 2015. The authors also examined relevant reference lists, and restricted inclusion to English-language peer-reviewed empirical articles.

items.question: What central construct did an eligible empirical article have to define or measure as a main aim or outcome?
items.explanation: A study focused only on improving end-of-life care did not qualify unless it also had the required definitional aim. The final review contained 36 articles using qualitative, quantitative, or mixed methods.

items.question: Which qualitative research tradition informed the consensus, co-occurrence, and comparison coding approach?
items.explanation: The authors generated themes, refined the coding scheme through discussion, and independently coded definitions. Disagreements were discussed, with a third author consulted when needed.

items.question: Which core theme included respect for someone as an individual and maintaining independence?
items.explanation: These were the subthemes used in this review. The discussion cautions that related concerns can be expressed under other themes, so article frequencies do not directly establish how much an individual values this concept.

items.question: What kappa value did the authors report for agreement between the independent coders?
items.explanation: The reported coefficient indicates agreement beyond chance under this measure. It does not establish the validity of a universal definition; the malformed p-value in the stored source is not used in this question.

items.question: How were studies treated with respect to sample-size weighting when their theme frequencies were summarized?
items.explanation: The authors did not apply weighting because they combined qualitative and quantitative work. These descriptive summaries should not be interpreted as pooled population preference estimates.

items.question: Which three stakeholder perspectives organized the definitions in this review?
accepted_answers: patients, family members, and healthcare providers
patients, healthcare providers, and family members
family members, patients, and healthcare providers
healthcare providers, family members, and patients
family members, healthcare providers, and patients
healthcare providers, patients, and family members
items.explanation: The groups contained 20 patient-perspective, 10 family-perspective, and 18 HCP-perspective articles. Some articles contributed to several groups, and the patient-perspective category included varied populations rather than only hospitalized dying patients.

items.question: Why do the three perspective-group counts add to more than the 36 unique articles?
items.explanation: Seven articles contributed to more than one perspective group. The groups are therefore not three mutually exclusive sets of unique studies.

items.question: What feature of the studies' methods and reporting prevented a formal meta-analysis?
items.explanation: Studies differed in assessment methods, depth of information, and reporting of participant characteristics. Descriptive aggregation does not remove these limitations or establish statistically significant differences between stakeholder groups.

items.question: Which core theme combined freedom from suffering with pain and symptom management?
items.explanation: This was a commonly reported theme. The results section and later discussion give conflicting broad frequency statements, so this question tests the theme rather than a disputed percentage.

items.question: Which broad theme included how, where, when, and with whom death occurs, as well as preparation for death?
items.explanation: It also included dying during sleep. Its frequent appearance across articles does not imply that everyone wants the same scene or preparation; the content concerns preferences.

items.question: Which theme included saying goodbye, feeling that life was well lived, and accepting death?
items.explanation: The authors identified this as one of the themes appearing across all three stakeholder groups. A shared category can still contain different personal meanings and priorities.

items.question: Which theme appeared in 70% of family-perspective articles, 35% of patient-perspective articles, and 22% of HCP-perspective articles?
items.explanation: This was the largest descriptive difference between groups in reported theme frequency. The denominators are articles in each perspective group; the pattern is not a measured percentage of individual people or proof that patients value it less.

items.question: What interval was generally unreported even though preferences might change as death approaches?
items.explanation: The authors identify the timing of interviews or surveys relative to death as a limitation. Without it, comparisons cannot adequately address how wishes may evolve near the end of life.

items.question: Which family perspective was poorly represented because most family studies took place after the death?
items.explanation: Most family articles involved bereaved relatives recalling a death. Their accounts should not automatically be treated as identical to the patient's own wishes or to family views before the loss.
